# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs,
tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual
setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.

I’ll inspect the snapshot structure, instructions, configs, launch path, data/reward code, and available metrics/evaluation artifacts, then write the required diagnosis only.

Wrote the diagnosis to [`agent_answer.md`](/user/user1/autorlbench-runs/20261114130450-00646d/workspace/$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md).

arguments.command: /bin/bash -lc "cat run.sh; printf '\\n-- log --\\n'; cat run/logs/seeds_15112943.out; printf '\\n-- rl script --\\n'; sed -n '1,240p' examples/math/gsm8k_rl.py; printf '\\n-- configs relevant --\\n'; for f in examples/math/gsm8k_{grpo_megatron,reinforce,ppo}.yaml; do echo ==== "'$f; cat $f; done'
/bin/bash -lc "find run -maxdepth 5 -type f | sed -n '1,200p'; echo '--- dirs'; find run -maxdepth 4 -type d"

/bin/bash -lc "rg -n \"class MathAgent|reward|extract|correct|trunc|eos\" areal examples | head -200; echo '--- end log'; tail -80 run/logs/seeds_15112943.out; echo '--- ktdump schema'; python - <<'PY'
import pandas as pd,glob
for f in glob.glob('run/ktdump/seeds_tis_c5_s1/kt_*.parquet'):
 d=pd.read_parquet(f); print(f, d.shape, d.columns.tolist()); print(d.head(1).to_dict('records'))
PY"

/bin/bash -lc "find . -type f | rg -v '("'^./'"\\.git|parquet|merges|out"'$)'"' | sort | tail -100; rg -n \"held|frozen|accuracy|pass@|eval\" . --glob '"'!run/logs/*'"' --glob '"'!*.yaml'"' | head -100"

/bin/bash -lc 'mkdir -p "$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS"; cat > "$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md" <<'"'EOF'
Verdict: **UNHEALTHY (incomplete run; held-out health is unestablished).**

The concrete failure is the 4-hour scheduler wall-time limit, not an optimization crash. "'`run.sh` describes a 3-epoch/87-step job, while the recorded log reaches only `Epoch 3/3 Step 7/29`, train step `65/87` (2026-11-08 06:41:24) and is then terminated at 06:44:16: `JOB 15112943 ... CANCELLED ... DUE TO TIME LIMIT`. Thus the fixed training budget was not completed and no final model/endpoint is evidenced.

There is also no usable frozen held-out evaluation result. The resolved configuration has `evaluator.freq_epochs: 1` and `freq_steps: null`, but the run never finishes epoch 3; the only recurring `timeperf/eval` entries are microsecond-scale bookkeeping values, and `eval-rollout.log`/`proxy-eval-rollout.log` contain no reported held-out accuracy/result. Therefore the rising training signal cannot establish health.

The optimization and rollout signals before cancellation are broadly numerically live: updates report `update_successful=1`, finite gradient norms (about 1.4–3.1), task reward rising from about 0.68 to 0.91, and importance-weight averages near 1. Rollouts are accepted. Some trajectories are long or lack EOS (`no_eos_ratios/avg≈0.0039`, max 1; incorrect sequences roughly 10–13% late in the run), but the logs do not show these causing the termination or a demonstrated held-out regression. They are symptoms/diagnostics, not established root causes. The root cause of the unhealthy staged experiment is the wall-time cancellation before the prescribed run and its corresponding held-out evaluation evidence.
EOF
cat "$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md"'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat, decoupled PPO with truncated importance sampling (TIS, cap 5) on GSM8K
# (AReaL, local scheduler). 3 epochs = 87 steps on one 8-GPU node: 4 SGLang rollout servers +
# 4 FSDP actor ranks (the allocation and every other default come from examples/math/gsm8k_icepop.yaml).
# The recorded run resolved the model and dataset by hub id from an offline cache
# (actor.path=Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat, dataset path openai/gsm8k, see config.yaml);
# here they point at the local copies that environment/prepare.sh places in the workspace.
# The recorded job had a 4-hour wall-clock limit.
set -euo pipefail
W="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "$W"
export PYTHONPATH="$W${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"

SEED="${SEED:-1}"
RLROOT="${RLROOT:-$W/run}"
MODEL_PATH="${MODEL_PATH:-$W/models/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat}"
DATA_PATH="${DATA_PATH:-$W/data/gsm8k}"
mkdir -p "$RLROOT/experiments" "$RLROOT/name_resolve" "$RLROOT/logs"

export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 HF_DATASETS_OFFLINE=1 HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1
export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
export AREAL_ALLOW_DEFAULT_ADMIN_KEY=1
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
# Per-token logprob dumps (inference-engine / proximal / current), every 20th call.
export KT_DUMP_DIR="$RLROOT/ktdump/seeds_tis_c5_s${SEED}"
export KT_DUMP_EVERY=20

python examples/math/gsm8k_rl.py \
    --config examples/math/gsm8k_icepop.yaml \
    experiment_name=kt-seeds \
    trial_name=tis_c5-s${SEED} \
    seed=$SEED \
    scheduler.type=local \
    cluster.fileroot="$RLROOT/experiments" \
    cluster.name_resolve.nfs_record_root="$RLROOT/name_resolve" \
    actor.path="$MODEL_PATH" \
    train_dataset.path="$DATA_PATH" \
    valid_dataset.path="$DATA_PATH" \
    actor.optimizer.lr=3e-6 \
    actor.optimizer.weight_decay=0.01 \
    ++actor.eps_clip=0.2 \
    ++actor.eps_clip_higher=0.28 \
    actor.mb_spec.max_tokens_per_mb=4096 \
    ref.mb_spec.max_tokens_per_mb=4096 \
    ++train_dataset.setup_timeout=900 \
    ++valid_dataset.setup_timeout=900 \
    ++rollout.setup_timeout=900 \
    total_train_epochs=3 \
    actor.rejection_sampling.action=clamp \
    actor.rejection_sampling.lower=1e-6 \
    actor.rejection_sampling.upper=5.0

    config, _ = load_expr_config(args, GRPOConfig)
    tokenizer = load_hf_tokenizer(config.tokenizer_path)

    train_dataset = get_custom_dataset(
        split="train",
        dataset_config=config.train_dataset,
        tokenizer=tokenizer,
    )
    valid_dataset = get_custom_dataset(
        split="test",
        dataset_config=config.valid_dataset,
        tokenizer=tokenizer,
    )

    workflow_kwargs = dict(
        temperature=config.gconfig.temperature,
        top_p=config.gconfig.top_p,
        max_tokens=config.gconfig.max_tokens,
        max_completion_tokens=config.gconfig.max_new_tokens,
    )
    eval_workflow_kwargs = workflow_kwargs.copy()
    eval_workflow_kwargs["temperature"] = 0.6

    with PPOTrainer(
        config,
        train_dataset=train_dataset,
        valid_dataset=valid_dataset,
    ) as trainer:
        trainer.train(
            workflow="areal.workflow.openai.math_agent.MathAgent",
            workflow_kwargs=workflow_kwargs,
            eval_workflow="areal.workflow.openai.math_agent.MathAgent",
            eval_workflow_kwargs=eval_workflow_kwargs,
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1:])

The concrete failure is the 4-hour scheduler wall-time limit, not an optimization crash. `run.sh` describes a 3-epoch/87-step job, while the recorded log reaches only `Epoch 3/3 Step 7/29`, train step `65/87` (2026-11-08 06:41:24) and is then terminated at 06:44:16: `JOB 15112943 ... CANCELLED ... DUE TO TIME LIMIT`. Thus the fixed training budget was not completed and no final model/endpoint is evidenced.

There is also no usable frozen held-out evaluation result. The resolved configuration has `evaluator.freq_epochs: 1` and `freq_steps: null`, but the run never finishes epoch 3; the only recurring `timeperf/eval` entries are microsecond-scale bookkeeping values, and `eval-rollout.log`/`proxy-eval-rollout.log` contain no reported held-out accuracy/result. Therefore the rising training signal cannot establish health.

The optimization and rollout signals before cancellation are broadly numerically live: updates report `update_successful=1`, finite gradient norms (about 1.4–3.1), task reward rising from about 0.68 to 0.91, and importance-weight averages near 1. Rollouts are accepted. Some trajectories are long or lack EOS (`no_eos_ratios/avg≈0.0039`, max 1; incorrect sequences roughly 10–13% late in the run), but the logs do not show these causing the termination or a demonstrated held-out regression. They are symptoms/diagnostics, not established root causes. The root cause of the unhealthy staged experiment is the wall-time cancellation before the prescribed run and its corresponding held-out evaluation evidence.
